zh.title: REGENT自主海洋翼地滑翔機Squire完成美軍演習測試
zh.summary: REGENT自主翼地滑翔機Squire於美軍演習完成測試，執行電子戰任務。
body: 美國載具製造商 REGENT 宣布，旗下自主研發的 Squire 海洋翼地滑翔機（Seaglider）已於美國密西根州舉行的「寂靜蜂群」（Silent Swarm）軍事演習中完成美軍運作測試。這項為期兩週的演習匯集了橫跨陸地、空中與海洋領域的實驗性無人系統，旨在評估各項平台於實戰環境中的整體表現。
在演習期間，Squire 自主翼地滑翔機搭載了專為電子攻擊、電子防護以及電子戰支援所設計的任務載荷。該平台與其他無人系統協同作業，並於複雜的電磁環境中接受測試，面臨包括雷達、無線電通訊、衛星導航、紅外線及定向能量系統等多種威脅與反制措施的考驗。
Squire 屬於翼地效應載具（Wing-in-ground vehicle），利用貼近水面飛行時產生的空氣動力效應提升運作效率。該載具保持於水面上約一個翼展的高度飛行，能有效低於雷達地平線，結合最高 70 節（約每小時 130 公里）的巡航速度與低雷達截面積特性，提供極高的戰術隱蔽性。
Squire 原型驗證機的大小約為 REGENT 旗下一型載客 Viceroy 滑翔機的四分之一，設計航程可達 100 海浬（約 185 公里）。REGENT 指出，這款被稱為 Squire USA-V 的無人水面與空中載具可承載達 23 公斤（50 磅）的任務載荷，適用於情報偵察、前線後勤、搜救以及反潛作戰等多種任務。
REGENT 於 2025 年 7 月正式成立專責的國防部門，積極推動翼地滑翔機技術從民用交通拓展至軍事與民防領域。公司目前正持續透過自研的飛控軟體開發全自主飛行能力，並同步規劃搭載混合動力系統的軍用版 Viceroy 載具，以延伸未來的執勤範圍與任務彈性。

en.title: REGENT Autonomous Squire Seaglider Completes Operations in US Military Exercise
en.summary: REGENT completed US military exercise operations with its autonomous Squire seaglider in Michigan.
body: US-based manufacturer REGENT has completed operations with the US military using its autonomous Squire seaglider during the Silent Swarm military exercise held in Michigan. The two-week exercise brought together experimental uncrewed systems operating across land, air, and maritime domains, providing a platform to evaluate new autonomous technologies in operationally relevant settings.

During the Silent Swarm exercise, the autonomous Squire seaglider was equipped with operational payloads designed for electronic attack, electronic protection, and electronic warfare support. The vehicle operated alongside other uncrewed platforms while being exposed to various electromagnetic threats and countermeasures, including radar, communications, navigation, infrared, and directed-energy systems in contested environments.

Squire is a wing-in-ground vehicle, also referred to as a ground-effect vehicle, that utilizes an aerodynamic phenomenon to fly at extremely low altitudes just above the water's surface. Operating within roughly a wingspan of the water and below the radar horizon, the platform is designed to combine high speeds of up to 70 knots (130 km/h) with a low radar signature.

The Squire demonstrator is approximately one-quarter the size of REGENT's passenger-carrying Viceroy Seaglider and is designed to operate over distances of up to 100 nautical miles (185 km). According to REGENT, the Squire USA-V platform can carry payloads of up to 23 kg (50 lb) to support missions such as intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, frontline logistics, search and rescue, and anti-submarine warfare.

To expand its presence in defence applications beyond commercial passenger transport, REGENT established a dedicated defence division in July 2025 to market the autonomous vehicle to military and civil defence operators. The company is also working on flight-control software for autonomous operations and developing a militarised hybrid variant of its larger Viceroy platform.

zh.title: 瑞士首架F-35A戰機組件於義大利開工組裝
zh.summary: 瑞士首架F-35A前機身與主翼於義大利開始組裝；預計2027年赴美培訓
body: 瑞士政府公布，其未來F-35A戰隊的首座前機身段與主翼，已於義大利卡梅里（Cameri）的 Leonardo 工廠展開組裝作業。該架軍用編號為 J-6004 的戰機，組件完成後將送往美國進行最終總裝，預計於2029年底交付瑞士。
依據當前規劃，瑞士預計首批8架F-35A戰機將直接於美國總裝，並於2027年中起部署至埃賓空軍基地（Ebbing Air Force Base）進行飛行員培訓。此後接收的戰機則預計於卡梅里廠區製造並直接交付瑞士，用以替換現役的 F/A-18 蜂式戰鬥機。

en.title: Assembly of Switzerland's First F-35A Fighter Components Begins in Italy
en.summary: Switzerland's first F-35A components enter assembly in Italy ahead of planned 2027 pilot training in US.
body: The first forward fuselage section and wing for Switzerland's F-35A fleet have entered assembly at Leonardo's Cameri facility in Italy. The aircraft, which will receive military registration J-6004, is scheduled for final assembly in Fort Worth, United States, and is expected to be delivered to Switzerland at the end of 2029.

Under current plans, the initial eight Swiss F-35As will be assembled in the United States and deployed to Ebbing Air Force Base from mid-2027 for pilot training. Switzerland intends to deploy its new F-35A fleet to replace its aging F/A-18 Hornet fighters.
